# 2022 FIFA World Cup knockout stage

The knockout stage of the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") was the second and final stage of the competition, following the [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup#Group_stage "2022 FIFA World Cup"). Played from 3 to 18 December, the knockout stage ended with the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2022 FIFA World Cup final"), held at [Lusail Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lusail_Stadium "Lusail Stadium") in [Lusail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lusail "Lusail"), [Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar "Qatar") between [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team "Argentina national football team") and [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_national_football_team "France national football team").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-match_schedule-1) The top two teams from each group advanced to the knockout stage to compete in a [single-elimination tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament"). There were 16 matches in the knockout stage, including a match for third place played between the two losing teams of the semi-finals.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-regulations-2) [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco_national_football_team "Morocco national football team") made history by becoming the first African and first Arab nation to reach a FIFA World Cup semi-final, defeating Spain and Portugal in the process.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-3)

## Format

The knockout stage of the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") was contested between 16 teams that qualified from the group stage. Matches in the knockout stage were played to a finish. If the score of a match was level at the end of 90 minutes of playing time, [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") was played. If, after two periods of 15 minutes, the scores were still tied, the match was decided by a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-regulations-2) All times listed are local in Arabia Standard Time ([UTC+3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC+03:00 "UTC+03:00")).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-match_schedule-1)

### Netherlands vs United States

The teams had previously met five times, with the Netherlands winning the first four encounters. They most recently met in a June 2015 friendly, with the United States winning 4–3.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-5)

Early on in the contest, [Christian Pulisic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Pulisic "Christian Pulisic") was sent through on goal for the United States but saw his shot saved by the outstretched leg of goalkeeper [Andries Noppert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andries_Noppert "Andries Noppert"). The Netherlands then went in front in the 10th minute, when [Memphis Depay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Depay "Memphis Depay") received a ball from the right from [Denzel Dumfries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denzel_Dumfries "Denzel Dumfries") and finished into the left corner of the net after a sequence of passes.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-6) In added time in the first half, [Daley Blind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daley_Blind "Daley Blind") made it 2–0 for the Dutch with another low finish, receiving the ball on the right from Dumfries for his second assist of the game. In the 76th minute, the United States pulled a goal back when [Haji Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haji_Wright "Haji Wright") finished with a deflection from [Christian Pulisic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Pulisic "Christian Pulisic")'s looped cross at the far post. Dumfries sealed the win with a third goal for the Netherlands five minutes later, adding to his two assists with a side-footed finish at the far post from Blind's cross.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-7)

### Argentina vs Australia

The teams had previously met seven times, with Argentina winning five, drawing one, and losing one of these encounters. The sides notably met in the [1994 FIFA World Cup inter-confederation play-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(OFC–CONMEBOL_play-off) "1994 FIFA World Cup qualification (OFC–CONMEBOL play-off)"), which Argentina won 2–1 on aggregate. They also faced off in [Argentina's 4–2 win](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Confederations_Cup_Group_A#Australia_v_Argentina "2005 FIFA Confederations Cup Group A") at the [2005 FIFA Confederations Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Confederations_Cup "2005 FIFA Confederations Cup"). Their most recent meeting was in a September 2007 friendly, with Argentina winning 1–0.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-10)

On his 1,000th career appearance, [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") scored his 789th career goal and first in a World Cup knockout stage, giving Argentina the lead in the 35th minute with a low left-footed finish into the left corner. [Julián Alvarez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julián_Alvarez "Julián Alvarez") made it 2–0 in the 57th minute when he pounced on an error by Australian goalkeeper [Mathew Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Ryan "Mathew Ryan") to finish low to the net past the stranded goalkeeper.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-11) Australia pulled a goal back in the 77th minute when [Craig Goodwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Goodwin "Craig Goodwin")'s strike took a huge deflection off [Enzo Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzo_Fernández "Enzo Fernández") and ended up in the right corner of the net.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-12) Australia had chances to level the match, first when [Aziz Behich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aziz_Behich "Aziz Behich") dribbled past four players before his shot was blocked by [Lisandro Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisandro_Martínez "Lisandro Martínez"), then in added time when [Garang Kuol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garang_Kuol "Garang Kuol") had a shot saved at close range by Argentine goalkeeper [Emiliano Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emiliano_Martínez "Emiliano Martínez"). Argentina also spurned several opportunities to add to their advantage, with substitute [Lautaro Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lautaro_Martínez "Lautaro Martínez") guilty of squandering multiple chances.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-13)

### France vs Poland

The teams had met sixteen times prior to this match, with France winning eight and Poland winning three of these encounters, along with five draws. Poland's three victories included the [1982 World Cup match for third place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Match_for_third_place "1982 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"), which they won 3–2. The sides most recently met in a friendly in June 2011, won by France 1–0.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-16)

After [Olivier Giroud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivier_Giroud "Olivier Giroud") missed a chance for France in front of goal off a cross from [Ousmane Dembélé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ousmane_Dembélé "Ousmane Dembélé"), Poland nearly opened the scoring later in the first half when [Piotr Zieliński](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piotr_Zieliński "Piotr Zieliński") saw two close-range shots blocked in quick succession. In the 44th minute, Giroud received a pass from [Kylian Mbappé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylian_Mbappé "Kylian Mbappé") before firing low to the right corner of the net to put France into the lead, in the process also breaking the [all-time French scoring record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_leading_goalscorers_for_the_France_national_football_team "List of leading goalscorers for the France national football team") with his 52nd goal for the nation. Mbappé made it 2–0 in the 74th minute, when he received the ball on the left just inside the [penalty area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_area "Penalty area") before firing powerfully into the top left corner of the net. Mbappé got his second of the game in the first minute of added time with a right-footed curling finish past goalkeeper [Wojciech Szczęsny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wojciech_Szczęsny "Wojciech Szczęsny"). In the final minute of the match, [Robert Lewandowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Lewandowski "Robert Lewandowski") pulled a goal back for Poland to make it 3–1 with a penalty low to the left corner, awarded after a handball by [Dayot Upamecano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayot_Upamecano "Dayot Upamecano"); goalkeeper [Hugo Lloris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Lloris "Hugo Lloris") saved Lewandowski's initial attempt, but it was retaken after Lloris was deemed to have left his goal line too early.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-17)

### England vs Senegal

The two teams had never met before.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-20) It was also the first time England faced an African opposition in the World Cup knockout stage since a [1990 quarter-final win over Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Cameroon_vs_England "1990 FIFA World Cup knockout stage").

After a tight opening period where Senegal's [Boulaye Dia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulaye_Dia "Boulaye Dia") saw his strike saved by goalkeeper [Jordan Pickford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Pickford "Jordan Pickford"), England went in front in the 38th minute, when [Jordan Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Henderson "Jordan Henderson") scored low into the net from twelve yards off a pass from [Jude Bellingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jude_Bellingham "Jude Bellingham") on the left. In added time in the first half, reigning [World Cup Golden Boot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_awards#Golden_Boot "FIFA World Cup awards") winner [Harry Kane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Kane "Harry Kane") made it 2–0 with his first goal of the tournament, firing into the net from the right after a pass from [Phil Foden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Foden "Phil Foden"). In the 57th minute, Foden crossed from the left for [Bukayo Saka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukayo_Saka "Bukayo Saka") to make it 3–0 with a clipped left-footed finish over Senegal goalkeeper [Édouard Mendy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Édouard_Mendy "Édouard Mendy").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-21)

### Japan vs Croatia

The teams had previously met three times, with a draw and a win for each side. Two of these encounters were in World Cup group stages: Croatia won [1–0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_H#Japan_vs_Croatia "1998 FIFA World Cup Group H") in 1998, and the teams drew [0–0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_F#Japan_vs_Croatia "2006 FIFA World Cup Group F") in 2006. The latter draw was the most recent encounter between the two.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-24)

In the 43rd minute, [Daizen Maeda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daizen_Maeda "Daizen Maeda") scored the opener for Japan with a low finish in the penalty area, after the ball was knocked back to him from the left. Ten minutes into the second half, [Ivan Perišić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Perišić "Ivan Perišić") equalised when he headed powerfully to the right corner of the net after a cross from [Dejan Lovren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dejan_Lovren "Dejan Lovren") on the right. The match saw no further goals scored either in the ninety minutes or during extra time and thus went to a penalty shoot-out. Japan missed three of their four penalties, with all three saved by goalkeeper [Dominik Livaković](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominik_Livaković "Dominik Livaković"). After [Marko Livaja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marko_Livaja "Marko Livaja")'s effort struck the post, [Mario Pašalić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Pašalić "Mario Pašalić") scored the winning spot kick with a low shot to the left, as Croatia won the shoot-out 3–1.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-25) Livaković became the third goalkeeper to make three saves in a [World Cup shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_FIFA_World_Cup_penalty_shoot-outs "List of FIFA World Cup penalty shoot-outs"), after [Ricardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_(footballer,_born_1976) "Ricardo (footballer, born 1976)") for [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team") in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#England_vs_Portugal "2006 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") and his fellow countryman [Danijel Subašić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danijel_Subašić "Danijel Subašić") in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Croatia_vs_Denmark "2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-26)

### Brazil vs South Korea

The teams had previously met seven times, with Brazil winning six and South Korea winning one of these encounters. The most recent meeting was in June 2022, a 5–1 friendly win for Brazil.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-29)

[Vinícius Júnior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinícius_Júnior "Vinícius Júnior") opened the scoring for Brazil in the 7th minute, when he converted a side-footed shot to the right of the net past three Korean defenders on the line. Brazil were awarded a penalty six minutes later when [Richarlison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richarlison "Richarlison") was fouled just inside the penalty area, which the returning [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") scored with a low shot to the right corner of the goalkeeper, who didn't move. Richarlison made it 3–0 in the 29th minute when he controlled the ball with his head before receiving the ball back from [Thiago Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiago_Silva "Thiago Silva") and passing into the left corner of the net. [Lucas Paquetá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Paquetá "Lucas Paquetá") got Brazil's fourth goal before half-time in the 36th minute, volleying low into the left corner of the net with his right foot after a cross from Vinícius Júnior on the left. In the second half, South Korea pulled a goal back when [Paik Seung-ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paik_Seung-ho "Paik Seung-ho") finished into the right of the net from thirty yards out. With ten minutes left and leading by three goals, Brazilian goalkeeper [Alisson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alisson_Becker "Alisson Becker") was substituted for third-choice keeper [Weverton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weverton_(footballer,_born_1987) "Weverton (footballer, born 1987)"), making Brazil the first team to ever play 26 different players in a single World Cup.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-30)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-31)

### Morocco vs Spain

The teams had met in three previous international matches, with two wins for Spain and one draw. Spain won both legs of the [1962 World Cup inter-continental play-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(CAF–UEFA_play-off) "1962 FIFA World Cup qualification (CAF–UEFA play-off)"), while the sides' most recent meeting was a [2–2 draw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_B#Spain_vs_Morocco "2018 FIFA World Cup Group B") in the 2018 World Cup group stage.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-34)

After a goalless 120 minutes that were dominated in possession by Spain but saw few chances created, the match went to a penalty shoot-out. Spain failed to convert any of their three attempts, with goalkeeper [Yassine Bounou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yassine_Bounou "Yassine Bounou") saving two of them from [Sergio Busquets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Busquets "Sergio Busquets") and [Carlos Soler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Soler "Carlos Soler"), and [Pablo Sarabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Sarabia "Pablo Sarabia") hitting the post, whilst Morocco scored three out of four, including the winning penalty from [Achraf Hakimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achraf_Hakimi "Achraf Hakimi") via a [panenka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panenka_(penalty_kick) "Panenka (penalty kick)") kick in the middle of the goal, seeing Morocco progress to the World Cup quarter-finals for the first time in history.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-35)

Morocco also became the first Arab country to reach the quarter-finals, and just the fourth African nation – after [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon_national_football_team "Cameroon national football team") in [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup "1990 FIFA World Cup"), [Senegal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senegal_national_football_team "Senegal national football team") in [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup "2002 FIFA World Cup"), and [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_national_football_team "Ghana national football team") in [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup") – to qualify for the last eight.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-36) Additionally, Morocco manager [Walid Regragui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walid_Regragui "Walid Regragui") became the first African and first Arab head coach to progress this far at a World Cup.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-37)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-38) Spain became just the second team to fail to convert a single attempt in a [World Cup penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_FIFA_World_Cup_penalty_shoot-outs "List of FIFA World Cup penalty shoot-outs"), after [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_national_football_team "Switzerland national football team") lost to [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine_national_football_team "Ukraine national football team") in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Switzerland_vs_Ukraine "2006 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") by exactly the same scoreline at the very same phase.

### Portugal vs Switzerland

The teams had met 25 times, with nine wins for Portugal, eleven wins for Switzerland, and five draws. The sides faced off in several editions of World Cup qualification, including [1938](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1938_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_Group_5 "1938 FIFA World Cup qualification Group 5"), [1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_–_UEFA_Group_1 "1970 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group 1"), [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_–_UEFA_Group_7 "1990 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group 7"), [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_–_UEFA_Group_1 "1994 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group 1"), and [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_–_UEFA_Group_B "2018 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group B"). Their most recent meeting was in June 2022, with Switzerland winning 1–0 in the [2022–23 UEFA Nations League A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022–23_UEFA_Nations_League_A#Group_2 "2022–23 UEFA Nations League A").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-41)

Captain [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") was left out of the starting line-up for Portugal – a first in major tournaments since their [UEFA Euro 2008 group stage defeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008_Group_A#Switzerland_vs_Portugal "UEFA Euro 2008 Group A"), also against Switzerland – with [Gonçalo Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonçalo_Ramos "Gonçalo Ramos") named instead to make his first start.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-42)

After Portugal took a 2–0 first-half lead via goals from Ramos and [Pepe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_(footballer,_born_1983) "Pepe (footballer, born 1983)"), Ramos would score a further two efforts – either side of goals by [Raphaël Guerreiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raphaël_Guerreiro "Raphaël Guerreiro") (assisted by Ramos) and Swiss defender [Manuel Akanji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Akanji "Manuel Akanji") – in the second half to become the first [hat-trick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_FIFA_World_Cup_hat-tricks "List of FIFA World Cup hat-tricks") scorer of the 2022 World Cup, the first player to score a hat-trick on their debut World Cup start since [Miroslav Klose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miroslav_Klose "Miroslav Klose") in [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_E#Germany_vs_Saudi_Arabia "2002 FIFA World Cup Group E"), and the youngest World Cup hat-trick scorer since [Flórián Albert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flórián_Albert "Flórián Albert") in [1962](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_4#Hungary_vs_Bulgaria "1962 FIFA World Cup Group 4"). A late long-range strike from substitute [Rafael Leão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Leão "Rafael Leão") concluded a 6–1 Portuguese victory as they reached the quarter-finals for the first time since [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Quarter-finals "2006 FIFA World Cup knockout stage").

The result equalled Switzerland's 5–0 defeat to [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") in [1966](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_FIFA_World_Cup "1966 FIFA World Cup") as their biggest ever World Cup loss. In getting Portugal's second goal, Pepe became the oldest player to ever score in the World Cup knockout stage,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-43) and the second-oldest to have scored at any stage of the World Cup, behind only [Roger Milla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Milla "Roger Milla"), who scored the consolation goal in [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon_national_football_team "Cameroon national football team")'s [thumping by the opposite scoreline in the 1994 group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_B#Russia_vs_Cameroon "1994 FIFA World Cup Group B") against [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_national_football_team "Russia national football team").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-44)

## Quarter-finals

### Croatia vs Brazil

The teams had met on four previous occasions, with three wins for Brazil and one draw. Two of these encounters took place in the World Cup group stage, with Brazil winning both matches: 1–0 in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_F#Brazil_vs_Croatia "2006 FIFA World Cup Group F") and 3–1 in [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_A#Brazil_vs_Croatia "2014 FIFA World Cup Group A").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-47)

Brazil created the majority of the game's chances, forcing Croatian keeper [Dominik Livaković](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominik_Livaković "Dominik Livaković") into eleven saves, the most in a single match at the tournament. Early in the second half, a handball in the Croatian penalty area by Croatian defender [Josip Juranović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josip_Juranović "Josip Juranović") was dismissed by the referee after being deemed accidental. Following a scoreless ninety minutes, [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") finally claimed the opener just before half-time of extra time with his 77th international goal, bringing him level with [Péle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Péle "Péle") as [the nation's all-time top scorer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team#Top_goalscorers "Brazil national football team"); after receiving the ball back from [Lucas Paquetá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Paquetá "Lucas Paquetá"), Neymar rounded Livaković and shot high into the net from the right side of the penalty area. A defensive lapse then cost Brazil their lead, as [Bruno Petković](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Petković "Bruno Petković") equalised for Croatia three minutes from the end; after picking out [Mislav Oršić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mislav_Oršić "Mislav Oršić")'s cross on the left flank, he fired a shot into the corner of the net that took a deflection off the leg of Brazilian defender [Marquinhos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquinhos "Marquinhos"). This would be Croatia's only shot on target of the game. In the subsequent penalty shoot-out, Croatia scored all four of their attempts, while Brazil's first kicker [Rodrygo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrygo "Rodrygo") had his shot saved by Livaković diving to his left, before Marquinhos hit his penalty low against the left post to confirm Brazil's elimination.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-48)

Croatia qualified for their second successive World Cup semi-finals and their third ever, while Brazil exited the tournament at the hands of a European team for the fifth consecutive edition; their [2002 World Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2002 FIFA World Cup final") triumph against [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") remained their last knockout stage win against European opposition. In the same period, Brazil was eliminated at the quarter-finals in all four World Cup tournaments they played away from home, thus excluding a fourth-place finish at the [2014 tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup") which they hosted.

### Netherlands vs Argentina

Main article: [Battle of Lusail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Lusail "Battle of Lusail")

See also: [Argentina–Netherlands football rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina–Netherlands_football_rivalry "Argentina–Netherlands football rivalry")

This was the tenth meeting between the teams, continuing a [historic rivalry among the two nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina–Netherlands_football_rivalry "Argentina–Netherlands football rivalry"). The Netherlands had won four of the previous nine encounters, Argentina had won one, and the remaining four matches were draws. The sides had faced off five previous times in World Cup matches; a 4–0 win for the Dutch in the [second group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_A#Netherlands_vs_Argentina "1974 FIFA World Cup Group A") in 1974 was replied to with a 3–1 Argentine victory in the [1978 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1978 FIFA World Cup final"). The Netherlands then won 2–1 in the [1998 quarter-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Netherlands_vs_Argentina "1998 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"), prior to goalless draws in the [2006 group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_C#Netherlands_vs_Argentina "2006 FIFA World Cup Group C") and the [2014 semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Netherlands_vs_Argentina "2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"), with the Argentines winning the latter meeting 4–2 on penalties.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-51)

[Nahuel Molina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nahuel_Molina "Nahuel Molina") opened the score for Argentina after 35 minutes, when he received a through ball in traffic from [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") and flicked it low past advancing goalkeeper [Andries Noppert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andries_Noppert "Andries Noppert"). In the 73rd minute, after [Marcos Acuña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_Acuña "Marcos Acuña") had been fouled in the penalty area by [Denzel Dumfries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denzel_Dumfries "Denzel Dumfries"), Messi scored the resulting penalty to the right of the net to double Argentina's advantage. After being subbed on by the Netherlands in the 78th minute, [Wout Weghorst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wout_Weghorst "Wout Weghorst") pulled a goal back just five minutes later, converting a downward header via a cross on the right from [Steven Berghuis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Berghuis "Steven Berghuis").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-52) He then scored an equaliser in the eleventh minute of added time, when a late Dutch free kick on the edge of Argentina's penalty area was played by [Teun Koopmeiners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teun_Koopmeiners "Teun Koopmeiners") directly to Weghorst as he stood in a decoy wall, sending the match to extra time. Argentina controlled the majority of the thirty-minute period, which saw [Enzo Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzo_Fernández "Enzo Fernández") strike the post in its dying moments, but the sides could ultimately not be separated and thus entered a penalty shoot-out, just as they had in 2014.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-53)

In the shoot-out, Argentine goalkeeper [Emiliano Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emiliano_Martínez "Emiliano Martínez") saved both of the Netherlands' first two attempts from [Virgil van Dijk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgil_van_Dijk "Virgil van Dijk") and Berghuis, as Argentina scored twice to earn a 2–0 advantage. After Fernández missed the chance to send his side through with their fourth penalty, [Lautaro Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lautaro_Martínez "Lautaro Martínez") scored Argentina's subsequent spot kick to end the shoot-out 4–3 in their favour and progress to the semi-finals.

There were a number of contested incidents between the sides both [during](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Lusail#Match "Battle of Lusail") and [after](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Lusail#Aftermath "Battle of Lusail") the match that [garnered much discussion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Lusail#Reception "Battle of Lusail"). Players clashed on multiple occasions across the contest, during both regulation and the subsequent shoot-out.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-54)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-55) Messi was also involved in confrontations with Dutch manager [Louis van Gaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_van_Gaal "Louis van Gaal") and an unwanted encounter with Weghorst during his post-match interview.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-56)

In total, the match saw a total of eighteen yellow cards brandished, breaking the World Cup record of sixteen that was set in another Dutch knockout defeat, their infamous [round of 16 game against Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Nuremberg_(2006_FIFA_World_Cup) "Battle of Nuremberg (2006 FIFA World Cup)") in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-Smith101222-57) Spanish referee [Antonio Mateu Lahoz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Mateu_Lahoz "Antonio Mateu Lahoz") received criticism for his failure to control the match, with many fans and media outlets considering his yellow cards to be too lenient for some instances that could have seen players sent off, while other incidents were ignored altogether.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-58) The amount of yellows issued by Mateu Lahoz was also criticised.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-59)

Because of these events, the match has been referred to as the "Battle of Lusail", in reference to the aforementioned 2006 contest between Portugal and the Netherlands that had been dubbed "The Battle of Nuremberg". The match continued the Netherlands' record of not losing a World Cup match since the [2010 World Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2010 FIFA World Cup final").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-60)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-Smith101222-57)

The match was also marred by the death of American sportswriter [Grant Wahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Wahl "Grant Wahl") after he collapsed near the end of the match while watching in the press box.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-Yeung-61)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-62)

### Morocco vs Portugal

The teams had met twice before, both during the World Cup group stage, with both sides winning one match: Morocco won 3–1 in [1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_F#Portugal_vs_Morocco "1986 FIFA World Cup Group F"), while Portugal prevailed 1–0 in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_B#Portugal_vs_Morocco "2018 FIFA World Cup Group B").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-65)

In the first half, [Youssef En-Nesyri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youssef_En-Nesyri "Youssef En-Nesyri") would put Morocco in front after 42 minutes when he jumped highest from a [Yahia Attiyat Allah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahia_Attiyat_Allah "Yahia Attiyat Allah") cross to head past advancing goalkeeper [Diogo Costa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diogo_Costa "Diogo Costa") and into the empty net, followed by [Bruno Fernandes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Fernandes "Bruno Fernandes")' attempted equalizer just before half-time striking the bar from long range. Portugal subbed on [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") in the second half, which saw him equal the [record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men's_footballers_with_100_or_more_international_caps "List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps") of 196 international caps set by [Bader Al-Mutawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bader_Al-Mutawa "Bader Al-Mutawa").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-66)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-67) Despite late Portuguese chances from [João Félix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/João_Félix "João Félix"), Ronaldo and [Pepe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_(footballer,_born_1983) "Pepe (footballer, born 1983)"), and the dismissal of Moroccan defender [Walid Cheddira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walid_Cheddira "Walid Cheddira") following two yellow cards in quick succession, Morocco would hold on to win 1–0.

With their victory, Morocco became both the first African and first Arab country to reach the World Cup semi-finals, as well as the second [Muslim-majority country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_world "Muslim world") after [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey_national_football_team "Turkey national football team") in [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Senegal_vs_Turkey "2002 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") to qualify for the last four.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-68) This was only the third time a nation from outside Europe and South America reached this stage after the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_soccer_team "United States men's national soccer team") in 1930 and [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea_national_football_team "South Korea national football team") in 2002.

### England vs France

The teams had previously met 31 times, with 17 wins for England, nine wins for France and five draws. Two of these meetings took place during the World Cup, with England winning on both occasions: they defeated France [2–0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_1#England_vs_France "1966 FIFA World Cup Group 1") in the [1966 group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_FIFA_World_Cup "1966 FIFA World Cup") and [3–1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_4#England_vs_France "1982 FIFA World Cup Group 4") in the [1982 first group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup "1982 FIFA World Cup"). The sides most recently met in a friendly in June 2017, with France winning 3–2.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-71)

[Aurélien Tchouaméni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurélien_Tchouaméni "Aurélien Tchouaméni") opened the scoring for France in the 17th minute, with a shot from outside the penalty area to the left corner which beat England goalkeeper [Jordan Pickford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Pickford "Jordan Pickford") diving down to his right. Several pundits questioned the goal because England's [Bukayo Saka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukayo_Saka "Bukayo Saka") had been brought to the ground, allowing France to win possession, in the build-up to the opener. Some claimed it was a clear foul, while others, including British journalists, thought the contact was not clear enough for the [VAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_assistant_referee "Video assistant referee") to overturn the on-pitch decision.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-72)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-73)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-74) Early in the second half, England were awarded a penalty after Tchouaméni fouled Saka inside the area. [Harry Kane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Kane "Harry Kane") scored from the spot against his club teammate [Hugo Lloris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Lloris "Hugo Lloris"), shooting to the left, which put Kane level with [Wayne Rooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Rooney "Wayne Rooney") as [England's all-time top scorer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team#Top_goalscorers "England national football team") at 53 goals. Just moments after seeing his volley saved by Pickford, [Olivier Giroud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivier_Giroud "Olivier Giroud"), who himself entered the match as France's all-time top scorer, also scored his 53rd international goal twelve minutes from time, with a header to the left of the net after a cross from [Antoine Griezmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoine_Griezmann "Antoine Griezmann"). In the 84th minute, the VAR awarded [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team "England national football team") a second penalty after English substitute [Mason Mount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Mount "Mason Mount") was seen being pushed over in the area by [Théo Hernandez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Théo_Hernandez "Théo Hernandez"). Kane again took the spot-kick but this time his shot blazed over the bar, as France held on to win 2–1 and progress to the last four, while England were eliminated in the World Cup quarter-finals for a record seventh time.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-75)

France became the first reigning world champions to reach the World Cup semi-finals since [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") in [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup#Semi-finals "1998 FIFA World Cup"), whom France would beat in that year's [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1998 FIFA World Cup final").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-76) France's passage to the semi-finals along with Croatia's, the side they defeated in the [2018 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2018 FIFA World Cup final"), marked the first time that both teams from a World Cup final reached the last four of the subsequent tournament since [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team "Argentina national football team") and [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") in [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup#Semi-finals "1990 FIFA World Cup").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-77) The referee [Wilton Sampaio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilton_Sampaio "Wilton Sampaio") had received criticism from many England fans, even resulting in the Wikipedia page for the referee as saying that he was called "A Brazilian Cheat"."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-78)

## Semi-finals

### Argentina vs Croatia

The teams had met five times before, each side winning twice and drawing once. Two of these matches took place in the World Cup group stage: a [1–0 win for Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_H#Argentina_vs_Croatia "1998 FIFA World Cup Group H") in [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup "1998 FIFA World Cup") was followed by [Croatia's 3–0 victory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_D#Argentina_vs_Croatia "2018 FIFA World Cup Group D") in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-81)

Both sides kept a cautious approach in the match's opening half hour, until Croatian defenders [Dejan Lovren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dejan_Lovren "Dejan Lovren") and [Joško Gvardiol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joško_Gvardiol "Joško Gvardiol") mistakenly let [Julián Alvarez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julián_Alvarez "Julián Alvarez") pass through the defence in the 32nd minute, leading to goalkeeper [Dominik Livaković](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominik_Livaković "Dominik Livaković") colliding with Alvarez. Referee [Daniele Orsato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniele_Orsato "Daniele Orsato") booked Livaković and awarded a penalty kick to Argentina, which [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") converted high into the top right corner of the goal. The collision also sparked a feud between Orsato and some Croatia players, causing [Mateo Kovačić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mateo_Kovačić "Mateo Kovačić") to be booked and the sending off of assistant coach [Mario Mandžukić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Mandžukić "Mario Mandžukić"). In the 39th minute, Alvarez ran through several Croatian defenders and scored Argentina's second goal. In the second half of the match, Croatian coach [Zlatko Dalić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zlatko_Dalić "Zlatko Dalić") substituted off five players, including team captain [Luka Modrić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modrić "Luka Modrić"), in order to boost the attacking ability of the team, but this didn't stop Messi and Alvarez from providing another goal for the Argentinians; in the 69th minute, Messi twisted past Gvardiol on the byline before teeing the ball up to Alvarez in the center, enabling Alvarez to score his second goal. The match ended in a 3–0 victory for Argentina, a reversal of the scoreline from their 2018 encounter.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-82)

Messi's goal from the penalty spot was his eleventh at a World Cup, taking him ahead of [Gabriel Batistuta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_Batistuta "Gabriel Batistuta") as Argentina's most prolific goalscorer in the competition. Messi also drew level with former German midfielder [Lothar Matthäus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lothar_Matthäus "Lothar Matthäus")'s record of [25 matches played in World Cup finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_players_who_have_appeared_in_the_most_FIFA_World_Cups#Matches "List of players who have appeared in the most FIFA World Cups").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-83)

### France vs Morocco

The teams had previously met seven times, with France winning five matches and the other two being draws. Their most recent encounter was a friendly in 2007, ending in a 2–2 stalemate. This was the first World Cup meeting between the sides.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-86) The match marked the first ever World Cup semi-final featuring either an African or Arab country, and just the third time that a team from a confederation outside Europe and South America played at this stage, after the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_soccer_team "United States men's national soccer team") in [1930](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1930_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Semi-finals "1930 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") and [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea_national_football_team "South Korea national football team") in [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Semi-finals "2002 FIFA World Cup knockout stage").

[Théo Hernandez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Théo_Hernandez "Théo Hernandez") would give France an early lead in the fifth minute, netting an acrobatic volley from a tight angle on the left after [Kylian Mbappé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylian_Mbappé "Kylian Mbappé")'s shot was diverted into his path. Hernandez's goal, timed at four minutes and 39 seconds, was the fastest in a World Cup semi-final since [Vavá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vavá "Vavá") netted in the second minute of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team")'s [5–2 win](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Brazil_vs_France "1958 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") against France in [1958](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_FIFA_World_Cup "1958 FIFA World Cup"). It was also just the second goal Morocco had conceded at the tournament and the first since the group stage.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-87) [Olivier Giroud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivier_Giroud "Olivier Giroud") would hit the post for France, before Moroccan captain [Romain Saïss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romain_Saïss "Romain Saïss") was forced to withdraw after 21 minutes, having been a doubt to start the match after going off injured in the quarter-finals. Morocco would then nearly equalise right before half-time, after [Jawad El Yamiq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawad_El_Yamiq "Jawad El Yamiq") saw his overhead kick strike the post and be cleared away. Despite being in possession of the ball for the majority of the contest, Morocco were not rewarded for this pressure, and after Mbappé dribbled into the penalty area in the 79th minute, his ball would find [Randal Kolo Muani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randal_Kolo_Muani "Randal Kolo Muani"), who scored his first-ever goal for France with his first touch of the game to double their advantage, having come on as a substitute 44 seconds prior.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-88)

France's 2–0 victory set up a final against Argentina, putting them one win away from becoming the first nation to successfully defend the World Cup since Brazil won the [1958](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_FIFA_World_Cup "1958 FIFA World Cup") and [1962](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_FIFA_World_Cup "1962 FIFA World Cup") editions.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-89)

## Match for third place

The teams had previously faced each other twice, including their opening game in [Group F](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_F "2022 FIFA World Cup Group F") at this World Cup, which ended [0–0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_F#Morocco_vs_Croatia "2022 FIFA World Cup Group F").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-92) This marked the second consecutive World Cup where the teams playing in the match for third place also played each other in the group stage, following [Belgium vs England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Match_for_third_place "2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup").

Croatia went in front with an early goal, after defender [Joško Gvardiol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joško_Gvardiol "Joško Gvardiol") diverted a diving header into the top left corner of the net in the seventh minute, assisted via a headed pass from [Ivan Perišić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Perišić "Ivan Perišić"). Croatia's lead would only last two minutes; Morocco's [Achraf Dari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achraf_Dari "Achraf Dari") received the ball after a [Hakim Ziyech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hakim_Ziyech "Hakim Ziyech") free kick struck the Croatian wall, and levelled the score in the ninth minute with a close-range header, having been left unmarked in front of the net.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-93) However, the *Vatreni* managed to regain the lead shortly before half-time through [Mislav Oršić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mislav_Oršić "Mislav Oršić"), who shot a long-range bending strike from just inside the penalty area on the left, hitting the inside of the post before the ball nestled in the back of the net.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-third-94) Although Croatian keeper [Dominik Livaković](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominik_Livaković "Dominik Livaković") was forced into a smothering save at close range to deny Morocco's [Youssef En-Nesyri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youssef_En-Nesyri "Youssef En-Nesyri"), the second half saw no further goals scored, handing Croatia a third-place finish at the World Cup for the second time, following the one achieved in [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Match_for_third_place "1998 FIFA World Cup knockout stage").

This was the [eleventh consecutive World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_nations_at_the_FIFA_World_Cup#Overview "European nations at the FIFA World Cup") in which a European team finished third, dating back to [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Match_for_third_place "1982 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"). Despite the defeat, a fourth-place finish still signified the best ever World Cup achievement for Morocco and an African team; they won more matches in the 2022 edition than in their first five World Cup appearances combined. Additionally, this achievement also matches the best finish by a team outside of UEFA or CONMEBOL since [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea_national_football_team "South Korea national football team") in [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup "2002 FIFA World Cup").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-95)

## Final

Main article: [2022 FIFA World Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2022 FIFA World Cup final")

The teams had met on twelve previous occasions, with Argentina winning six matches, France three, and the other three ending in draws. The sides had faced each other three times in the World Cup, with two of these encounters coming in the group stage: Argentina won [1–0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1930_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_1#Argentina_vs_France "1930 FIFA World Cup Group 1") in [1930](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1930_FIFA_World_Cup "1930 FIFA World Cup") (their World Cup debut) and [2–1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_1#Argentina_vs_France "1978 FIFA World Cup Group 1") in [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_FIFA_World_Cup "1978 FIFA World Cup"), while their most recent World Cup meeting was France's [4–3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#France_vs_Argentina "2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") victory in the [2018 round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Round_of_16 "2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"), their first defeat of Argentina since 1986.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-98)

Both teams were seeking to win a third World Cup title. France were the first [title holders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2018 FIFA World Cup final") to play in the final since [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team"), whom France defeated as hosts in [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1998 FIFA World Cup final"), and were aiming to become the first nation to retain the World Cup since Brazil's victories in [1958](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_FIFA_World_Cup "1958 FIFA World Cup") and [1962](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_FIFA_World_Cup "1962 FIFA World Cup"). French coach [Didier Deschamps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Didier_Deschamps "Didier Deschamps") was attempting to become the second manager to win multiple World Cup titles, and the first since [Vittorio Pozzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vittorio_Pozzo "Vittorio Pozzo") in [1934](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1934_FIFA_World_Cup "1934 FIFA World Cup") and [1938](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1938_FIFA_World_Cup "1938 FIFA World Cup") with [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team"). Argentina, who had been defeated by [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") in both of their previous two trips to the final (in [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1990 FIFA World Cup final") and [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2014 FIFA World Cup final")), were looking for a first world title in 36 years, having last won the competition in [1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_FIFA_World_Cup "1986 FIFA World Cup").

Following a dominant first half that saw Argentina go up 2–0 thanks to a [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") penalty and a goal from [Ángel Di María](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ángel_Di_María "Ángel Di María"), they were suddenly caught out late into the second period with two goals in two minutes for France from [Kylian Mbappé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylian_Mbappé "Kylian Mbappé"). After the match headed to extra time, Messi would score his second to regain Argentina's lead, only for Mbappé to again equalise two minutes from time via his second penalty, making him the first player since [Geoff Hurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Hurst "Geoff Hurst") in [1966](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_FIFA_World_Cup_final "1966 FIFA World Cup final") to score a [hat-trick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_FIFA_World_Cup_hat-tricks "List of FIFA World Cup hat-tricks") in a World Cup final.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-OptaJean-99) Having scored once in the [2018 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2018 FIFA World Cup final"), Mbappé also became the first player to score four World Cup final goals, as well as the first player to reach eight goals in a single World Cup since [Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronaldo_(Brazilian_footballer) "Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)") for winners Brazil in [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup "2002 FIFA World Cup"). However, Mbappé failed to emulate Hurst's and Ronaldo's successes; despite him scoring the first attempt for France, they lost 4–2 in the [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_FIFA_World_Cup_penalty_shoot-outs "List of FIFA World Cup penalty shoot-outs") after [Kingsley Coman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsley_Coman "Kingsley Coman") and [Aurélien Tchouaméni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurélien_Tchouaméni "Aurélien Tchouaméni") failed to convert their efforts, with [Gonzalo Montiel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonzalo_Montiel "Gonzalo Montiel")'s spot kick sealing Argentina's victory.

Argentina achieved their third world title, surpassing France and [Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguay_national_football_team "Uruguay national football team")'s totals. They also became the first non-European side to win the title since Brazil in 2002, the previous occasion that the World Cup was held in Asia. With this victory, they became the second South American team to win a World Cup held entirely in Asia, after Brazil in 2002 when it was held in South Korea and Japan. France's loss was their second in a World Cup final, having been defeated by Italy in [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2006 FIFA World Cup final"), a match which was also decided by penalties.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-100) Many reporters, pundits and fans regarded the match as the greatest FIFA World Cup final of all time.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-101)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-102)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-103)

Both the tournament and the final itself saw Messi break multiple World Cup records. The match, which was his 26th overall in World Cup finals, saw him surpass [Lothar Matthäus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lothar_Matthäus "Lothar Matthäus") as the player with the [most appearances in the competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_players_who_have_appeared_in_the_most_FIFA_World_Cups#Matches "List of players who have appeared in the most FIFA World Cups"). His goals against France also made him the first player to score in all five rounds of a World Cup since the group stage to round of 16 format was introduced in 1986. Messi was subsequently named the final's official [Player of the Match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_of_the_Match "Player of the Match"), before being awarded the [Golden Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_awards#Golden_Ball "FIFA World Cup awards") for best player of the tournament.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-104) His five Player of the Match titles in 2022 were the [most ever won at a single World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_awards#Player_of_the_Match "FIFA World Cup awards") by a player since their introduction in 2002, and his Golden Ball award made him the first player to claim the accolade in multiple World Cups, having done so previously in 2014.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#cite_note-105)

**82nd Golden Globe Awards – Television Winners Report**  
*Held on January 5, 2025, the 82nd Golden Globe Awards honored American television productions of 2024. Below are the winners in all television categories.*

---

### Television Series Categories
| Category | Winner | Platform |
|----------|--------|----------|
| **Best Television Series – Drama** | **Shōgun** | FX / Hulu |
| **Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy** | **Hacks** | Max (HBO Max) |

### Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television
| Category | Winner | Platform |
|----------|--------|----------|
| **Best Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television** | **Baby Reindeer** | Netflix |

### Stand‑Up Comedy on Television
| Category | Winner | Special |
|----------|--------|---------|
| **Best Performance in Stand‑Up Comedy on Television** | **Ali Wong** – *Ali Wong: Single Lady* | Netflix |

### Lead Acting Performances
| Category | Winner | Role / Show |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| **Best Actor in a Television Series – Drama** | **Hiroyuki Sanada** | Lord Yoshii Toranaga – *Shōgun* (FX/Hulu) |
| **Best Actress in a Television Series – Drama** | **Anna Sawai** | Toda Mariko – *Shōgun* (FX/Hulu) |
| **Best Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy** | **Jeremy Allen White** | Carmen “Carmy” Berzatto – *The Bear* (FX/Hulu) |
| **Best Actress in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy** | **Jean Smart** | Deborah Vance – *Hacks* (Max) |

### Limited Series Lead Performances
| Category | Winner | Role / Show |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| **Best Actor in a Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television** | **Colin Farrell** | Oswald “Oz” Cobb / The Penguin – *The Penguin* (HBO/Max) |
| **Best Actress in a Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture Made for Television** | **Jodie Foster** | Chief Liz Danvers – *True Detective: Night Country* (HBO/Max) |

### Supporting Performances
| Category | Winner | Role / Show |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| **Best Supporting Actor on Television** | **Tadanobu Asano** | Kashigi Yabushige – *Shōgun* (FX/Hulu) |
| **Best Supporting Actress on Television** | **Jessica Gunning** | Martha Scott – *Baby Reindeer* (Netflix) |

---

**Key Takeaways**  
- **Shōgun** was the most successful television series, winning four awards (Best Series, Actor, Actress, Supporting Actor).  
- **Hacks** and **Baby Reindeer** each earned two wins.  
- The remaining series (*The Bear*, *The Penguin*, *True Detective: Night Country*) and stand‑up special (*Ali Wong: Single Lady*) each took one award.  

*Source: 82nd Golden Globe Awards Wikipedia page (television winners section).*

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Brody "Adrien Brody"), Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* star [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") was the first [trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") nominee for a Golden Globe motion picture acting category, for the [Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") category.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-12) [Jacques Audiard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Audiard "Jacques Audiard"), the director and writer of the film, was one of the most nominated individuals, with a total of three nominations: [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), and co-lyricist of [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") nominee "[El Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal_(song) "El Mal (song)")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7) The composers and co-lyricists of the song, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_(French_singer) "Camille (French singer)") and [Clément Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clément_Ducol "Clément Ducol"), tied Audiard for most nominated individuals. Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* is the first [Latvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_language "Latvian language") film to win [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17) [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") became the first [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese") actress to win a Golden Globe in an acting category,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) as well as the first Brazilian, first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and first [Portuguese-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") actor to win the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) She acknowledged her mother [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro")'s nomination, for *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")* (1998), in the same category at the [56th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Golden_Globe_Awards "56th Golden Globe Awards").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18)

*Emilia Pérez* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* were the biggest winners of the night, for film and television, respectively, with four wins each.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* was the next biggest film recipient, with three wins; for television, *[Baby Reindeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Reindeer "Baby Reindeer")* and *[Hacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacks_(TV_series) "Hacks (TV series)")* each won two.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19)
